bib.title: Diverse Beam Search: Decoding Diverse Solutions from Neural Sequence Models
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v2, 22 Oct 2018; the cited AAAI 2018 paper is the shorter 'Improved Description of Complex Scenes' version)

question: Can beam search be changed to return a list of diverse high-quality sequences without extra compute, and does that improve top-1 and oracle quality?
hypothesis: Optimising a diversity-augmented objective across groups of beams yields more diverse and better lists than plain beam search or earlier diversity heuristics.
contributions: Diverse Beam Search, a doubly greedy (over time and groups) approximate inference algorithm
Results on image captioning, visual question generation and machine translation
Analysis of image complexity vs gain from diversity, with a human preference study
Sensitivity analysis of G, lambda and diversity function

method.summary: Beam budget B is split into G groups of B'=B/G; groups are decoded left to right in order, each group running beam search on log-probs plus lambda times a dissimilarity to earlier groups' choices (Hamming by default). Compared to BS, Li & Jurafsky 2016 and Li et al. 2015 on captioning, VQG and En-Fr MT with oracle accuracy and distinct n-grams.
method.task: diverse decoding for neural sequence models (captioning, VQG, MT)

datasets.name: COCO
datasets.split: Karpathy & Fei-Fei public splits; 5000 test images implied by bin sizes 745+3416+839

datasets.name: PASCAL-50S
datasets.split: test only, except 200 validation images for tuning

models.name: neuraltalk2 captioner (Vinyals et al. 2015) and VQG variant
dl4mt-tutorial attention NMT (Bahdanau et al. 2014)
models.architecture: bidirectional GRU encoder with attention, decoder

models.name: SVR difficulty predictor
models.architecture: Support Vector Regressor on ResNet features

inference.decoding: Diverse Beam Search; baselines BS, Li & Jurafsky 2016 intra-sibling rank, Li et al. 2015 MMI-style U(y) penalty
inference.samples: B=20 returned sequences per input; no seeds or repeated runs stated

parameters.G: G=B=20 for reported results; G=1 is plain BS
parameters.lambda: grid searched on validation set per task; 0.2 to 0.8 works well; exact chosen values not stated in text
parameters.diversity_function: Hamming (best); also cumulative (temperature Gamma), n-gram, neural-embedding (word2vec)
parameters.delta: sum over beams in group of sequence dissimilarity; Eq 3 sums over earlier groups h<g with lambda_g

metrics.name: Oracle accuracy @k
metrics.definition: max of task metric (SPICE for captions/VQG, sentence BLEU-4 for MT) over k list members

metrics.name: Distinct n-grams
metrics.definition: count of distinct n-grams in the list divided by total words generated

metrics.name: Human preference
metrics.definition: forced choice DBS vs BS captions, majority vote of 5 turkers

eval.protocol: single run per configuration, no significance tests stated; own reimplementation of the baselines; lists sorted by log-prob, no reranker

limits: No variance, seeds or significance tests reported; gains are small in absolute SPICE/BLEU terms.
Models are 2015-era LSTM/GRU captioners and NMT; no Transformer or LLM experiments.
MT: DBS is not best on every oracle column (Li et al. 2015 higher at @10 and @20).
Baselines are the authors' own reimplementations; Li & Jurafsky / Li et al. use re-rankers originally, dropped here.
Oracle metrics measure the best of 20, which rewards diversity by construction; top-1 gains are small.
lambda values per task are not printed; sensitivity shown only in figures.
Dissimilarity is token-level; authors note initial words dominate diversity.
Table 2 Li & Jurafsky VQG row appears to copy COCO values.

terms.definition: Oracle or top-k accuracy for some task-specific metric like BLEU is the maximum value of the metric over a list of k potential solutions.
beam budget divided into G groups with a dissimilarity term between groups, optimised doubly greedily over time and groups

code.snippet: Y^g_[t] = argmax over y^g_1..y^g_B' of sum_b [ Theta(y^g_b,[t]) + sum_{h=1}^{g-1} lambda_g Delta(y^g_b,[t], Y^h_[t]) ] s.t. distinct, lambda_g >= 0
